err.legacyTitle: This {0} file can’t be played on this TV
err.legacyHint:
The container opened but your TV’s hardware decoder doesn’t recognise the codec inside.  {0} files from the late-90s / 2000s usually carry DivX, Xvid, WMV9 or similar — Samsung TVs only decode H.264, HEVC and a handful of others natively.

Three ways to play these:
  1. Set up the companion Tessel transcode server (recommended for SMB shares): a small Go binary you run once on a Linux box, Windows PC, Mac mini, NAS or Proxmox VM.  Pair it from Settings → Transcode server, and from then on every file streams through it — TV-incompatible codecs get transcoded on the fly, everything else passes through untouched.  See {1} (transcode-v* assets).
  2. Stream via Plex or Jellyfin if you already run one — they transcode server-side too, just hand the URL to Open Network Stream.
  3. Re-encode once with HandBrake or ffmpeg:
       {2}
err.mkvHint:
The MKV container itself is fine on this TV — the problem is a track inside it.  Most often that’s DTS or TrueHD audio, which Samsung TVs can’t decode (they only pass those through to an AV receiver over HDMI).  Less often it’s AV1 or 10-bit HEVC video.

Try, in order:
  1. Open the CC / track menu and pick another audio track (many releases include an AC3 or AAC track alongside the DTS one).
  2. Set up the companion Tessel transcode server: a small Go binary on any Linux box, Windows PC, Mac mini, NAS or Proxmox VM.  Pair from Settings → Transcode server; from then on TV-incompatible audio gets remuxed to AC3/AAC on the fly, video copied untouched.  See {0} (transcode-v* assets).
  3. Re-encode just the audio yourself (fast even on a Pi):
       {1}
